sections.h2: What should a seller know about Paulding County, Georgia?
sections.html:
Paulding is a fast-growing western suburb of metro Atlanta. Dallas is the county seat, and the government offices sit together on Constitution Boulevard. The Census Bureau's mid-2025 estimate is 190,996 people, a 13.3 percent gain on the 168,630 in its 2020 base. That is the largest population of the four Georgia counties in this comparison, packed into 312.35 square miles of land.

The housing numbers explain why sales here move at a different pace than in rural south Georgia. Half of owner-occupied Paulding homes are worth more than $326,300 (a 2020 to 2024 estimate), and 80.8 percent of households own where they live. Permits issued in 2025 totaled 1,326, and the median gross rent was $1,772 a month. A seller in the newer subdivisions competes with new construction, which sets buyer expectations for finishes and age of systems. Workers travel a mean of 39.6 minutes to their jobs, a sign that many residents commute toward Atlanta.

For a seller, the tax side is simple in outline. Value is fixed on January 1, taxed at 40 percent of that figure, and the commissioner multiplies by the millage. The commissioner's general information page explains the sequence. What follows concentrates on points that come up when a Paulding County house is sold.

sections.h2: Which Paulding County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
The assessors and the tax commissioner divide the job between them, and deeds sit with a third office. The Board of Assessors sets values, takes homestead applications and hears the first level of appeals. The tax commissioner bills and collects. The Clerk of Superior Court, in the courthouse, keeps recorded deeds.

Where to reach Paulding's tax commissioner and assessors, from the county's own pages

The commissioner's page warns that the phone line may be cut off early so the office can close at 4:00 p.m. The assessors accept homestead applications by email at the address printed on the county's homestead page, and the board's public meetings run on Wednesdays at 10 a.m. in the third-floor conference room.

sections.h2: What is the Paulding County property tax deadline, and what does missing it cost?
sections.html:
On the commissioner's general information page, the deadline is November 15 every year. The site's FAQ still shows December 4 for tax year 2024, which differs from the general page, so let the bill itself guide your payoff and closing plans.

The general information page spells out what happens after the deadline:

  • Interest posts to the account on the 16th of every month, calculated as prime plus 3 percent spread over twelve months.
  • A FIFA, which is the county's lien filing, is recorded at the Clerk of Superior Court's office thirty days after the delinquent notice date, and credit bureaus can read it there.
  • Penalties of 5 percent land at the 120-day mark and recur on that cycle until they reach 20 percent in total.
  • Accounts that stay unpaid are turned over to a contractor, and administrative and levy fees of $215 or more can be added to prepare the parcel for tax sale.

A mobile home follows its own calendar. Mobile home bills normally mail near January 2, fall due April 1 and pick up a 10 percent penalty the next day.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Paulding County assessment?
sections.html:
Paulding gives owners six and a half weeks, measured from the mailing of the notice. The county says a late filing cannot be accepted, so mark the envelope date when the notice arrives. Grounds are limited to whether the parcel is taxable, what it is worth and whether that value is fair next to similar homes. Anger about the millage or the total on the bill will not carry an appeal.

The path through the system runs in a fixed order:

  • Send the appeal to the Board of Assessors first, which re-checks its number and replies with a decision.
  • No deal at that stage means a hearing before the Board of Equalization.
  • Arbitration is the alternative to that board, and the assessors' staff can walk you through it.
  • If you are still unhappy after that decision, the next step is Superior Court.

The assessors keep an appeals page with a form, a 2026 guide to reading the notice, and a list of 2025 sales used for comparison. Someone serving abroad can have a relative or friend file for them, with 90 days instead of 45. Mobile home owners have the same 45 days to declare a different value.

sections.h2: What homestead exemptions can a Paulding County owner claim?
sections.html:
A Paulding County homeowner must apply with the Board of Assessors, because exemptions are never granted automatically. Expect to show residency and citizenship papers, for example a Georgia license or ID card, and your name has to be on the deed. You can claim a homestead on only one property, including property in other counties or states.

The county's homestead page names several categories beyond the standard exemption:

  • Lower school tax for owners aged 65 or more.
  • Relief for owners with a total and permanent disability.
  • A break for veterans rated fully disabled from service.
  • A full homestead break for the unmarried survivor of a peace officer or firefighter killed on duty.
  • An added exemption for homes inside the city limits of Hiram, approved by that city's voters in 2017.

Eligibility turns on owning and occupying the home on January 1. The assessors say applications must arrive by April 1, while the homestead page ties the current-year deadline to the appeal deadline on that year's assessment notice, so file as early as you can. A change in ownership, marriage, divorce or death requires a fresh application with the supporting paperwork. Farmland and timber programs come with a covenant that runs at least 10 years, so a seller of acreage should read the agreement before listing.

sections.h2: What happens to Paulding County property tax when a house sells?
sections.html:
Your purchase agreement spells out how the year's bill is shared with the buyer, and the settlement statement shows the result.

Request a balance figure from the commissioner before the sign goes up, including any interest, penalty or lien recorded against the parcel. A balance still open comes out of your proceeds, which hands the buyer a parcel with nothing owing. If the sale happens after a November due date but before the bill is paid, confirm in writing who pays it.

After closing, the new owner should make a fresh homestead application, because a change in ownership ends the old one. The seller can notify the assessors that the exemption no longer applies. The courthouse deed room can supply a copy of your recorded deed, which the buyer's title work will want.

faqs.q: What is the property tax due date in Paulding County?
faqs.a: The commissioner's general information page says November 15 each year. The site's FAQ still names a December date for the 2024 tax year, so go by the bill in your hands.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Paulding County property value?
faqs.a: Call the Board of Assessors at 770-443-7606. The tax commissioner at (770) 443-7581 handles billing, payments and payoff figures, not values.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal in Paulding County?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the notice mailing. The county states that appeals cannot be filed after that period ends.

faqs.q: Does Paulding County homestead exemption renew by itself?
faqs.a: Yes. After approval it carries over from year to year until the owner moves, the title changes or a different exemption is sought. A buyer starts a new application after closing.

faqs.q: What does Paulding County charge on late property tax?
faqs.a: Interest is charged monthly, and a penalty layer stacks on after four months. Its ceiling is one fifth of the tax, so a long-ignored Dallas-area bill grows quickly.
